**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject noncanonical typed artifact bytes**

When a valid Family delta—or, through the analogous projection parser below—is reserialized with different whitespace or key ordering and its receipt/path references are updated, `json.loads` and the semantic checks still accept it. Those raw bytes cannot be produced by the frozen #1766 canonical serializer, so the custody gate can authenticate an artifact that is not the claimed exact producer output; compare each parsed typed artifact's raw bytes with `canonical_bytes(document, CanonicalSerializationPolicy())` before admitting it.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Limit each successor to one appended Family**

For a non-rollback successor containing two or more newly reviewed Family deltas, this prefix-only check accepts the chain because it imposes no upper bound on the number of appended bindings. The frozen release contract permits only one new unique Family per successor, so multiple additions can be collapsed behind one predecessor link and lose their required per-Family release/review boundary; reject successors whose binding count grows by more than one.

This admits a summary that the #1766 producer cannot generate and violates the exact typed projection contract; validate every summary leaf as an `int` excluding `bool` before comparing counts.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject deltas that require semantic normalization**

When a canonically serialized delta contains unsorted QP/MS evidence references or unsorted QuestionPart records, this call silently normalizes those lists before comparing the cumulative projection, so a correspondingly normalized projection is accepted. The #1766 builder performs that normalization before serializing the delta itself, meaning the admitted raw delta could not be an exact producer output even after the byte-canonicality check above is added; verify that the normalized records equal the original delta records instead of accepting the mutated form.
